sources.title: M. Lortkipanidze, Arab rule in Georgia, Georgian Encyclopedia
sources.note: Direct original read: 697 Egrisi alignment; 735 to 736 campaign; taxes and public obligations; uneven control; regional principalities around the eighth/ninth-century transition. Do not adopt the article’s polemical modern national vocabulary.

sources.title: Jamshid Giunashvili, ABḴĀZ, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct original read, historical paragraphs on sixth to tenth centuries and 1008. Leo II episode explicitly attributed to Christian chronicles. Older article’s modern Soviet political judgements are not used.

sources.title: Lortkipanidze, Murgulia, Diasamidze and Khutsishvili, Egrisi clothing accessories of the sixth to eighth centuries, Chronos 5
sources.note: Original institutional English abstract directly read; issue 2024, published 20 January 2025. Buckles, clasps, pins, contexts and analogies. Authors propose military and exchange connections; individual ethnicity is not established by accessory type.

sources.title: Everill and colleagues, Forty seasons of excavation: Nokalakevi to Tsikhegoji to Archaeopolis, Iberia-Colchis 13 (2017), 146 to 165
sources.note: Full author-uploaded article directly read. Pages 146 to 147: inherited fortifications, river tunnel, late antique buildings. Page 152: reservoir and fifth/sixth-century bathhouse; seventh to eleventh-century ceramic groups. These buildings are not re-dated to the eighth century.

sources.title: Everill and colleagues, Scientific techniques at Nokalakevi, Anatolian Studies 71 (2021), 29 to 45
sources.note: Full author-uploaded original directly read; DOI 10.1017/S006615462100003X. Table 4 and diet discussion distinguish samples dated 610 to 690 and 660 to 770 CE; cemetery section rejects automatic assignment of an adult burial to the 551 attack. No claim that bone chemistry reconstructs a precise menu.

sources.title: Nato Chitishvili, Tsromi, Courtauld Crossing Frontiers
sources.note: Direct original read. Early seventh-century architecture; triangular niches; contemporary mosaic/fresco; eighth-century Rajden inscription dated by letter forms. Identification of a martyrdom location remains interpretation.

sources.title: Tbilisi State University, Tsromi, Church of the Ascension, Georgian Wall Painting
sources.note: Direct fetch failed; full indexed institutional text checked with exact query site:arthistory.tsu.ge/murals/architecture/tsromi-ascension-church "Ⴜ" "Holy" on 22 September 2026. Date 620s to 630s; construction inscription on south facade, original-script scholarly transcription and translation. Parentheses indicate editorial expansion. No independent visual epigraphic reading claimed.

sources.title: A. Bogveradze, Abo Tbileli, Georgian Encyclopedia
sources.note: Direct original read: Abo skilled at mixtures from myrrh, service to Nerse II, Baghdad to Kartli and Khazar journey, conversion and execution in 786. Tbilisi lies outside this record’s polygon; narrative is contextual and hagiographic. Exact disputed feast/day not used.

sources.title: John Sabanisdze, Georgian Encyclopedia
sources.note: Direct fetch failed; full indexed original read via exact site query with "786" and "epistle". Work composed 786 to 790 at Catholicos Samoel’s request, letters prefaced it; received from a tenth-century manuscript. Do not turn the author’s education into evidence of universal schooling.

proposedOverrides.name: Georgian lands in the eighth century
proposedOverrides.summary: Eighth-century Georgian regional powers, distinct from the united kingdom established in 1008.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Separate contextual card, no alias association.
batchIdentityNotes.reason: The exact imported record predates unified Georgia. Western/southwestern footprint is neither all Kartli nor all the later Abkhazian kingdom. Tsromi and Nokalakevi are inside the approximate bounds; Tbilisi outside. Modern records inherit misleading kingdom aliases but are excluded.
batchIdentityNotes.evidenceLimits: Older baths/churches/child burial are explicitly dated as inherited or preceding evidence. No medieval household toilet, medicine recipe or universal schooling is inferred. No claim of independent visual transcription of Tsromi; indexed scholarly original with translation checked.
